parts: Hello. What do you know about SAT?

If by “SAT” you mean the U.S. college admissions test, it’s a standardized exam administered by urlCollege Boardhttps://www.collegeboard.org and used by many colleges and universities as one part of the admissions process.

The current SAT is fully digital and consists of two main sections:

- Reading and Writing
  - Reading comprehension
  - Grammar and language conventions
  - Vocabulary in context
  - Analysis of written passages

- Math
  - Algebra
  - Advanced math
  - Problem-solving and data analysis
  - Geometry and trigonometry

Key facts:
- Total score range: 400–1600
- Reading and Writing: 200–800
- Math: 200–800
- Test length: about 2 hours and 14 minutes
- The test uses adaptive modules, meaning performance in the first module influences the difficulty of the second.

Many schools in the United States are currently test-optional, meaning applicants may choose whether to submit SAT scores, though some institutions have reinstated testing requirements.

The SAT is often used for:
- College admissions
- Merit scholarships
- Academic placement in some programs

Preparation methods include:
- Official practice tests from urlBluebookhttps://bluebook.collegeboard.org
- Practice questions through urlKhan Academyhttps://www.khanacademy.org/digital-sat
- Commercial prep courses and tutoring
